TZA.note: No AI-specific harm rule or authority is stated; only general data protection duties on automated decisions.
Nothing stated on government use of AI.

facts.fact: Clyde & Co states that Tanzania has not yet enacted specific legislation regulating the use of AI.

TZA.note: No sectoral AI system in public use is stated.
No locally built AI model, dataset or computing is stated.

facts.fact: Clyde & Co lists the Cybercrimes Act, Chapter 443 Revised Edition 2023, among the laws that may apply to AI use in Tanzania.
Clyde & Co says the Personal Data Protection Act, Chapter 44 Revised Edition 2023, imposes general obligations on entities processing personal data, including through AI systems.
facts.system: Personal Data Protection Act, Cap. 44 R.E. 2023

facts.fact: Clyde & Co cites the Personal Data Protection (Personal Data Collection and Processing) Regulations, GN No. 449C of 2023, as imposing obligations alongside the Act.
facts.system: Personal Data Collection and Processing Regulations, GN 449C of 2023

facts.fact: Clyde & Co treats the Personal Data Protection Act, Cap. 44 R.E. 2023, and GN No. 449C of 2023 as the operative framework governing AI-driven processing of personal data.
facts.system: Personal Data Protection Act, Cap. 44 R.E. 2023

facts.fact: Clyde & Co says entities must comply with cross-border data transfer requirements under sections 31 and 32 of the PDP Act and regulations 20 to 22 of the Collection and Processing Regulations.
facts.system: PDP Act ss. 31-32; GN 449C of 2023 regs 20-22

TZA.note: The Electronic Transactions Act is only listed as possibly applicable; the document does not say what it provides.
No national ID system is described.
Nothing stated on public bodies sharing data.
